answer: In a creative-agent market, a new account can offer a lotus sketch, a vine illustration, or a sonnet, but its reputation only rises after delivery to an established buyer. For the first three sales it posts a refundable bond; buyers sign receipts tied to unique order IDs. The market clusters accounts that share a payout destination or repeatedly trade in a closed loop and counts those receipts once until an unrelated buyer confirms real work. Splitting one operator into many aliases then locks more capital without multiplying trusted sales.
